'''Arnab Rai Choudhuri''' is an Indian astrophysicist and writer known for his contributions to [[magnetohydrodynamics|Astrophysical magnetohydrodynamics]], specially in context of solar magnetic cycle.

== Biography==
He obtained his Bachelor of Science in 1978 from [[Presidency University, Kolkata|Presidency College]], [[University of Calcutta]] and his Master of Science in physics from the [[Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur]].

He earned his Ph.D. at the [[University of Chicago]] in 1985 working under the supervision of [[Eugene Parker]]. For then went on to research at the [[High Altitude Observatory]] for two years. In 1987, he joined the Physics Department of [[Indian Institute of Science]] (IISc) as a lecturer and was appointed as a full professor in 2002.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=http://insaindia.org/detail.php?id=P11-1537 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304090922/http://insaindia.org/detail.php?id=P11-1537 |url-status=dead |archive-date=4 March 2016 |title=Professor AR Choudhuri |publisher=[[Indian National Science Academy]] |access-date=27 January 2014 }}</ref><ref name=":1">{{cite web | url=http://www.physics.iisc.ernet.in/~arnab/ | title=Arnab Rai Choudhuri | publisher=IISC | access-date=27 January 2014}}</ref>

==Research==
Choudhuri then went on to work as a visiting scientist at various institutes and observatories around the world, from [[Isaac Newton Institute|Isaac Newton Institute, Cambridge]] to his alma mater [[University of Chicago]].<ref name=":1" />

Choudhuri runs a research group at the Indian Institute of Science which mainly deals with the study of magnetohydrodynamics, focusing on sunspot and solar magnetic cycle modelling.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Chatterjee | first1 = P. | last2 = Nandy | first2 = D. | last3 = Choudhuri | first3 = A. R. | doi = 10.1051/0004-6361:20041199 | title = Full-sphere simulations of a circulation-dominated solar dynamo: Exploring the parity issue | journal = Astronomy and Astrophysics | volume = 427 | issue = 3 | pages = 1019 | year = 2004 | arxiv = astro-ph/0405027 | bibcode = 2004A&A...427.1019C | s2cid = 1809622 }}</ref> He is a fellow of [[The World Academy of Sciences]] and the [[Indian National Science Academy]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sciences (TWAS) |first=The World Academy of |title=Choudhuri, Arnab Rai {{!}} TWAS |url=https://twas.org/directory/choudhuri-arnab-rai |access-date=2025-09-16 |website=twas.org |language=en}}</ref> In 2022, he was selected as the 9th Laureate of Chandrasekhar Prize of Plasma Physics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=UChicago Alumnus Professor Arnab Rai Choudhuri selected as 9th Laureate of Chandrasekhar Prize of Plasma Physics {{!}} News {{!}} Department of Astronomy and Astrophysics {{!}} The University of Chicago |url=https://astrophysics.uchicago.edu/news/article/prof-arnab-rai-choudhuri-uchicago-alumnus-is-selected-as-9th-laureate-of-s-chandrasekhar-prize-of-plasma-physics/ |access-date=2025-09-16 |website=astrophysics.uchicago.edu}}</ref>

== Selected Publications ==

=== Books ===
Choudhuri has authored the following books:

* Choudhuri, A. R. (1998) ''The Physics of Fluids and Plasmas: An Introduction for Astrophysicists,'' Cambridge University Press. {{ISBN|9781139171069}}
* Choudhuri, A. R. (2010) ''Astrophysics for Physicists'' Cambridge University Press.
* Choudhuri, A. R. (2015) ''Nature's Third Cycle: A Story of Sunspots'' Oxford University Press.
